what.text: This page follows refugees from Burundi in all host countries combined.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 318291 Burundian refugees, and the United Republic of Tanzania hosts the largest share, 41.2%.
Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda are the next largest hosts.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Burundi in several periods since 1965.
From 1994 to 2006 the groups fighting the government include the CNDD, Palipehutu-FNL and the CNDD-FDD, at war level in 1997 and from 2000 to 2002.
Later periods include 2014 to 2015 and 2019 to 2024, with RED-TABARA among the opposing groups.

when.text: UNHCR's figure peaked at 871376 in 1993 and fell to 72477 by 2014.
The main years of displacement in the data are 1993, 1997 to 2005 and 2017, and the figure changed sharply between 2014 and 2015.
Returns to Burundi were highest in 1994 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees; asylum seekers from Burundi are counted in a separate series.
People displaced inside Burundi are counted separately by UNHCR and by IDMC, and their figures are never added.
The sources don't say which routes people took.
